item.name: OAuth2 Social Login
item.description:
OAuth2 flows are browser-driven — Spring Security handles the authorization code exchange automatically.

Flow:
1. Open the initiation URL in a browser (not Postman) — it redirects to Google/GitHub consent page.
2. After consent, Google/GitHub redirects back to `/login/oauth2/code/{provider}`.
3. Spring Security exchanges the code, `CustomOAuth2UserService` finds/creates the DB user, `OAuth2AuthenticationSuccessHandler` issues JWT cookies and redirects to `auth.oauth2.redirect-uri` (default: http://localhost:3000/oauth2/callback?login=success).
4. The frontend reads the `access_token` cookie — identical to a form-login session.

The requests below can be used to verify the initiation redirect is reachable. Postman cannot complete the full browser-based flow.

item.name: Service-to-Service (S2S)
item.description:
Internal endpoints protected by HTTP Basic auth on `/api/internal/**`.

Other microservices (catalog-service, order-service, etc.) authenticate using their `client-id` and `client-secret` from `auth.service-clients.clients` in application config. Secrets use DelegatingPasswordEncoder prefix — `{noop}` for dev plaintext, `{bcrypt}` for production.

**No internal controllers are implemented yet** — the security chain is wired and ready. Add controllers under `/api/internal/**` and they will be protected automatically.

These requests use `{{s2s_client_id}}` and `{{s2s_client_secret}}` from the environment.

item.name: Filters & Interceptors
item.description:
Requests that exercise the cross-cutting filter and interceptor pipeline directly.

Execution order per request:
1. AuditRequestContextFilter (Servlet Filter @Order 1) — resolves/generates X-Correlation-Id, captures IP + User-Agent into ThreadLocal
2. Spring Security filter chain — HTTP Basic (Order 1, /api/internal/**) or JWT (Order 2, /api/**)
3. JwtAuthenticationFilter — validates JWT, checks DB blacklist, sets SecurityContext
4. ShallowEtagHeaderFilter — computes ETag on response body for GET requests
5. ClientIpInterceptor (MVC Interceptor) — puts User-Agent in MDC + RequestContext ThreadLocal
6. DBInterceptor (AOP @Before) — sets DbContextHolder to READ or WRITE before service methods
7. AuditAspect (AOP @Around @AuditAction) — times the call, persists AuditLog on success/error
8. ClientIpInterceptor afterCompletion — clears MDC + RequestContext ThreadLocal

exec: pm.test('Status 401 — exception path of AuditAspect ran', () => {
console.log('AuditAspect catches the thrown exception and persists:');
console.log('  Query: SELECT * FROM user_audit.audit_log WHERE action=\'USER_LOGIN\' AND status=\'ERROR\' ORDER BY audit_date DESC LIMIT 1;');

request.description:
AuditAspect wraps the call in try/catch. On exception it persists the AuditLog with status=ERROR and the truncated exception message. The exception is then re-thrown so GlobalExceptionHandler still returns 401.

Verify: SELECT * FROM user_audit.audit_log WHERE action='USER_LOGIN' AND status='ERROR' ORDER BY audit_date DESC LIMIT 1;

exec: pm.test('Status 200 — read pool served this GET', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

request.description:
GET /user/me → UserServiceImpl.getProfile() which is annotated @ReadOnly. DBInterceptor (@Before) sets DbContextHolder=READ → RoutingDataSource.determineCurrentLookupKey() returns DbType.READ → query goes to read-pool-dev (HikariCP).

Verify in server logs: the Hibernate SQL log line should show pool 'read-pool-dev'.

POST /user/register → UserServiceImpl.register() which is annotated @WriteOnly. DBInterceptor sets DbContextHolder=WRITE → RoutingDataSource routes to write-pool-dev (master DB).

Verify in server logs: the Hibernate INSERT SQL should use pool 'write-pool-dev'.
